chunks: From him, from Ya'qub, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from the one who mentioned him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I said to him, or we said: 'A partner (of ours) rejects our testimony.' He said, then he said: 'Do not humble yourselves.'

key_terms.شَرِيكاً: Partner (in a business or legal context, often referring to a non-Shia or person of another sect)
key_terms.لَا تُذِلُّوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ: Do not humble yourselves (i.e., do not feel belittled or consider your status lower because of their rejection)

ai.seo_question: Does a non-Shia partner's rejection of our testimony invalidate it in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In the context of *tahdhib al-ahkam*, this hadith addresses the jurisprudential concern of whether the testimony of Shias is invalidated by the rejection of a *sharik* (partner, often interpreted as a non-Shia or rival sect). Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) responds with 'Do not humble yourselves,' a directive that emphasizes maintaining self-worth and confidence in the validity of one's own testimony despite external opposition, rather than seeking validation from those who may be biased. This reflects the Shia scholarly principle of *istighna* (self-sufficiency) in legal matters, where the internal validity of the witness is not contingent upon the approval of the opposing party.
